blocks.text: I can explain that the digits in the numbers 11 to 19 express position on a number line.

items.title: Finding numbers on a number line
Estimating numbers on a number line

blocks.text: Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: One more than is when there is a greater amount by one or another item in the set.
One less than is when there is a smaller value by one.
To find a value that is close enough to the right answer, usually with some careful thought involved.

slides.title: Teen numbers on a number line

blocks.text: Let’s count from 10 to 20.
The teen numbers are between 10 and 20. They start with the digit 1, which represents 1 ten.
On the number line there is one big jump of 10. The teen numbers are an extra jump on from 10 up to 20.
Teen numbers are made of ten and a bit. We can say:

items: 11 is made of one ten and one one
12 is made of one ten and two ones
13 is made of one ten and three ones
14 is made of one ten and four ones
15 is made of one ten and five ones
16 is made of one ten and six ones
17 is made of one ten and seven ones
18 is made of one ten and eight ones
19 is made of one ten and nine ones

blocks.text: Saying a teen number as one ten and some ones helps you to find it on a number line.
Look at the one-digit numbers and the teen numbers.

blocks.label: Tap to see
blocks.text: The teen numbers all start with the digit 1. They end in the same digit as the one-digit numbers.
So we can use the numbers 1 to 9 to help us find the teen numbers on a number line.
What number comes next? How do you know?

items: One more than 1 is 2, so one more than 11 is 12.
One more than 4 is 5, so one more than 14 is 15.
One more than 7 is 8, so one more than 17 is 18.

blocks.text: If one more than 7 is 8, then 18 must be one more than 17.
We can use one more and one less to put numbers in order.

items: 15 is one more than 14.
13 is one less than 14.
17 is one more than 16.
15 is one less than 16.

blocks.text: We can say it in two ways: 12 is one more than 11, or 11 is one less than 12.

items.q: One more than 3 is 4. So what is one more than 13?

blocks.text: Where is 15 on the number line?

items: 15 comes between 14 and 16.
14 is one less than 15.
16 is one more than 15.

blocks.text: We can use one more, one less or in between to find where a number goes.

blocks.q: Match each number to the two numbers it comes between.

items.q: 17 is made of one ten and how many ones?
19 is made of one ten and how many ones?

blocks.text: 15 is halfway between 10 and 20. It is the **midpoint**.
The midpoint can help us to mark the other teen numbers.
When we estimate, we ask: is the number before or after the midpoint?

items: A number before the midpoint could be 14.
A number after the midpoint could be 16.

blocks.text: We can also ask which number it is nearer to.

items: 11 is nearer to 10. It is one more than 10.
19 is nearer to 20. It is one less than 20.

blocks.text: The midpoint is 15.

blocks.q: A number is more than 15 but less than 20. Which number could it be?
blocks.why: 17 is more than 15 and less than 20. 12 and 10 are less than 15.
19 is one less than 20, so it is nearer to 20.

blocks.q: Is 11 before or after the midpoint?
blocks.why: 11 is less than 15, and it is nearer to 10.

items: The numbers 11 to 19 can be positioned on a number line.
Saying the teen numbers as one ten and some ones helps you to position them.
There is a link between the position of the numbers 1 to 9 and the numbers 11 to 19.
Knowing one more and one less than a number to 20 can help to estimate the position of the teen numbers.

17 is one more than 16 and one less than 18.
One more than 3 is 4, so one more than 13 is 14.
19 is one more than 18, so one less than 19 is 18.
